note: Search-routing TUNING set, authored 2026-09-29 by the search router's writer; it fits search_router's cut-offs and is not evidence. search_holdout.json, written blind by another agent, decides (tools/route_eval.py --search).
reader_note: Labelling policy. Each request is labelled with the cheapest provider that still answers it well. tinyfish: the whole answer sits on one or two ordinary public pages (one fact, hours, a definition, a price a page shows, what one named page or doc says, a simple comparison from a few spec pages), and a page up to an hour old is fresh enough. perplexity: anything that needs many sources weighed together (reviews, 'best', pros and cons), news or events of today or this week, anything changing by the minute (a live score, a coin price), several searches one after another, or a vague request; and every doubt, because it is the safe default. firecrawl: live structured data a data service holds and is asked with fields: fares or hotel prices for a route or place AND dates, or a lookup in an official register or records database. A flight fact with no dates (a flight's length) is a page read; a fare with no route and dates (an average fare) is perplexity. 'surface' says whether the text is a query the brain wrote (brain) or the owner's task for the web reader (reader); 'tricky' marks the borderline cases.
